sections.intro: GitHub swapped a remote LLM pipeline for a compact encoder to detect secrets with higher throughput and less noise.

stories.title: GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
stories.summary: GitHub built a two-stage secret scanner: regexes generate candidate strings, then a fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier reads each candidate with its file path and surrounding code to filter false positives. Exported to ONNX with 8-bit quantization, it raised owner-weighted alert acceptance by 11.5%, cut median post-push scan time by 86%, and reduced serving cost by over 98% compared with the prior LLM pipeline.
stories.why: Concrete example of replacing a remote LLM pipeline with a compact encoder model for high-throughput classification at scale.
stories.takeaway: For classification over short, structured context, a fine-tuned compact encoder usually beats a general LLM on latency and cost.

sections.name: papers
sections.label: Papers
sections.intro: Ember oversubscribes GPU memory for large LLM inference on stock hardware, while ProvQML reframes training as recursive SQL tracking data lineage.

stories.title: Ember: Making Unified Virtual Memory Practical for Discrete-Memory GPUs
stories.summary: NVIDIA's Unified Virtual Memory slows down once data exceeds GPU memory because page-fault-driven migration wastes bandwidth and leaves the GPU idle. Ember starts allocations in host RAM and uses GPU hardware counters to promote only hot regions, batch-evicting cold ones. At 1.5x oversubscription it beats UVM by 6.8-10.6x on six apps and generates LLM tokens 4.7-16x faster at sizes where manual placement cannot run at all.
stories.why: Practical GPU memory oversubscription enables large LLM inference on stock GPUs without manual data placement.
stories.takeaway: Tracking page hotness via hardware counters, rather than prefetching on faults, is what makes automatic GPU memory management viable.

stories.title: ProvQML: Efficient Provenance Capture for Machine Learning as Recursive Aggregate SQL [Extended Version]
stories.summary: ProvQML extends a distributed recursive aggregate SQL engine to run ML algorithms as queries, capturing fine-grained provenance: local provenance ties each training instance to its gradient contribution at a specific step, while global provenance links the sequence of parameter updates across iterations. Experiments on standard ML datasets demonstrate efficient provenance capture for multiple model types.
stories.why: It turns ML training into recursive SQL queries while automatically tracking where every parameter update came from.
stories.takeaway: Recursive aggregate SQL is a viable execution layer for ML with built-in explainability through query provenance.

sections.name: tools
sections.label: Tools
sections.intro: An eleven-year soundness hole in Rust's borrow checker and a lightweight Rust TUI Spotify client exposing playback over an agent protocol.

stories.title: 11 year old unsoundness bugs found in Rust borrow checker
stories.summary: A bug in Rust since at least version 1.18 (2017) allows assigning a shorter-lived reference to a field that should require a 'static lifetime, by exploiting how variance interacts with field assignment and Drop. Exploitation requires a malicious Drop implementation, and AddressSanitizer catches the resulting use-after-scope. The Types Team is treating it as P-high and folding the fix into Project Zero.
stories.why: A long-standing soundness hole in Rust's borrow checker let lifetime bounds be bypassed, affecting any Rust codebase that relies on it for memory safety.
stories.takeaway: Even mature, formally-grounded type systems can hide soundness bugs for over a decade when variance, lifetimes, and destructors interact subtly.

stories.title: Show HN: Spotatui, a Spotify TUI/GUI without web API rate limits
stories.summary: spotatui is a Rust terminal music player forked from spotify-tui that streams Spotify natively via librespot, avoiding web API rate limits. It routes audio from multiple sources (YouTube, Subsonic, local files, Qobuz, Apple Music) through its own engine with an FFT visualizer and Lua plugins. It exposes a Model Context Protocol interface so coding agents can drive playback directly.
stories.why: Demonstrates a Rust TUI's lightweight footprint (~78 MB RAM) and exposes playback control over MCP for coding agents.
stories.takeaway: Bundling native streaming plus an MCP interface shows how to make a tool scriptable by agents without wrapper services.

sections.name: discussions
sections.label: Discussions
sections.intro: Anthropic's git replacement and a distributed GPU scheduler built from idle Apple Silicon devices.

stories.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
stories.summary: Anthropic built Scion, a server-centric VCS, after merge volume hit 30,000 per day and their monorepo reached roughly 100 GB of history. It uses content-addressed changesets in a write-ahead log, Spanner for ref state, recursively computed derived data, and stateless cache servers answering sparse checkout requests.
stories.why: Real case study of replacing git with a server-centric VCS to handle AI-driven merge volume in a massive monorepo.
stories.takeaway: For always-online workloads, a server-centric VCS with content-addressed storage and lazily derived data can outperform gits decentralized model.
stories.debate: Commenters question whether a monorepo at all is wise and whether announcing unreleased internal tools is useful, while others argue reinventing VCS becomes rational as AI lowers coding costs.

stories.title: A Dynamic and Distributed Virtual GPU Cloud Built on Idle Apple Silicon Devices
stories.summary: Minions pools idle Apple Silicon GPUs from macOS machines to run distributed ML inference. It manages task scheduling across devices with fault tolerance and input/output storage, avoiding new GPU procurement. Built as a response to high costs and wait times on centralized GPU infrastructure.
stories.why: Aggregates idle macOS GPUs into a cluster for ML inference, exploring fault tolerance and resource scheduling tradeoffs.
stories.takeaway: Harnessing idle consumer GPUs for inference requires weighing real costs versus centralized GPU clusters.
stories.debate: Commenters question whether the contribution is novel beyond a basic CRUD database plus S3. Others argue energy costs and inefficiency on consumer devices outweigh benefits compared to centralized data centers.

sections.name: offbeat
sections.label: Off the clock
sections.intro: A 1988 NeXT spreadsheet modeled data with categories instead of fixed grids, foreshadowing pivot tables and relational thinking.

stories.title: Lotus Improv on the NeXT
stories.summary: Lotus Improv was a NeXT-exclusive spreadsheet that replaced generic A1/B7 cell addresses with user-defined categories and items, letting formulas read like English and views rearrange on the fly. NeXTSTEP later became macOS and iOS. The author runs it today through Previous on Windows 11.
stories.why: A 1988 spreadsheet modeled data with named categories instead of fixed cells, foreshadowing pivot tables and relational thinking.
stories.takeaway: Decoupling data values from their layout makes analysis more intuitive; conventional spreadsheets remain stuck in a weaker 1980s model.
stories.debate: Commenters wonder how feasible it would be to rebuild Improv's relational model as a modern spreadsheet alternative in 2026.
